name: Corteva
description: Corteva sells seed and crop protection chemicals to farmers worldwide (2025 net sales $17.4B: North America 52%, Latin America 22%, EMEA 18%, Asia Pacific 8%). Seed (Pioneer and other brands) is the bigger and more profitable half: farmers buy new seed every planting season, and Corteva earns extra from licensed traits such as Enlist. Crop protection sells herbicides, insecticides and fungicides, and about 60% of sales fall in the first half of the year around planting. Corteva announced on Oct 1, 2025 that it will split into two public companies, New Corteva (crop protection) and a seed company to be named Vylor, expected in Q4 2026.

sub.name: Farm inputs: fertiliser, seeds and farm machinery

gics.note: Conventional GICS label as shown in Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (sector and sub-industry columns only; that list does not give industry group or industry). Read 2026-09-30.

businessLines.name: Seed
businessLines.how: Farmers buy hybrid and trait-enabled seed every season at a price per bag or unit, with trait fees and licensing; Corteva pays third-party growers to multiply the seed.
businessLines.description: Corn, soybean, sunflower, cotton and other seed with traits, sold through the Pioneer agency model, regional brands, retail and direct channels.

businessLines.name: Crop Protection
businessLines.how: Farmers and distributors buy chemicals per acre treated each season; generics and raw material costs drive price, and new active ingredients earn premium pricing.
businessLines.description: Herbicides, insecticides, nematicides, fungicides, seed treatments and nitrogen management.

brands.name: Pioneer, Brevant, PhytoGen, Enlist, Isoclast and others
brands.note: Brands named in 10-K; no per-brand sales given
